summary: Grading is a pure, integer-valued function of the four submitted plan files and static, SHA-256-pinned verifier fixtures; no randomness, clock, network, filesystem ordering, hash-seed dependence or readiness wait can change the grade of a fixed submission.

files_read: environment/app/tools/check_plan.py (byte-identical to tests/check_plan.py per manifest SHA-256)
environment/app/days/day-1.json (lines 1-60 read; all four day files scanned by grep for section layout, non-integer numerics, NaN/Infinity/null)

checks_performed: Traced tests/test.sh: fixed reward file, mktemp -d run dir (scratch only, never compared), python3 -I pytest with -p no:randomly and -p no:cacheprovider; reward derived solely from pytest exit code.

Traced tests/test_outputs.py: reads /app/plans/<day>.json (STAND_PLANS unset in grading), verifier-owned targets.json, roster.json and gzip day copies; each day copy is SHA-256 checked against the roster, whose hashes equal the manifest hashes of environment/app/days/day-N.json, so the evaluated day bytes are fixed on every run.

Traced tests/check_plan.py evaluate(): pure function over dicts/lists; no random, time, os.listdir/glob, or set iteration that affects the result; occupancy is explicitly sorted before buffer checks; cost is an integer sum.

Grep over all environment/app/days/*.json and all packet JSON found no decimal/exponent numerics and no NaN/Infinity/null, so cost arithmetic is exact integer arithmetic independent of summation order.
Checked target comparison: integer cost <= integer target from a static verifier-owned file; no tolerance or float boundary.

Checked dependency pinning: both images pin python:3.13-slim-bookworm by digest; verifier pins pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2; verifier runs with no network; no remote data is read at grading time.

Checked timing: evaluation is linear-ish in transfers plus quadratic only in widebody turns per wingtip pair (hundreds of turns), far below the 1800 s verifier timeout; no sleeps or service readiness waits exist.

Checked solution: solve.sh copies static saved plans and re-checks them; search.py (seeded random.Random, wall-clock budget) is not run by solve.sh, so its nondeterminism cannot affect Oracle or grading.
Checked environment Dockerfile apt-get install (unpinned tmux/asciinema/ca-certificates): affects only the agent image tooling, never the separate verifier image or grading inputs.

coverage_sweep.reason: Verifier uses only committed fixtures (four gzip day copies pinned by roster SHA-256, static targets). No random module or generator in tests. The only randomness in the packet is solution/search.py's seeded RNG, which solve.sh does not execute.
All graded inputs are the same four fixed days every run; the target boundary (cost <= target) is evaluated on fixed data with integer comparison, so no draw can include or omit a case.

No date/time use in tests/test_outputs.py or tests/check_plan.py; turn times are fixed minutes-from-midnight integers in the day data. time.time() appears only in solution/search.py, which is not run during grading or by solve.sh.
Base images pinned by digest; verifier pip packages pinned to exact versions; checker is a local stdlib-only file; verifier network_mode no-network; all grading inputs are local files under /tests.

coverage_sweep.category: Filesystem or iteration ordering; sorted where contract requires order
coverage_sweep.reason: Plans are read by explicit path per day, not by directory listing. Contract allows turn lists in any order; checker sorts occupancy by (arrive, depart, tid) before buffer checks, and wingtip clash check is order-independent, so equivalent orderings grade identically. Dict iteration is insertion-ordered and hash-seed independent; sets are used only for membership. Error message choice may depend on plan order but does not change pass/fail.
All day data numerics are integers (grep found no decimals/exponents), bus cost and walk matrix are integers, so the cost sum is exact regardless of order. Contract states costs are whole numbers.
No services, sleeps, or waits. Checker is fast relative to the 1800 s verifier timeout; no race between candidate and verifier since no candidate code runs in the verifier.

coverage_sweep.category: Repeated clean-run stability of correct and incorrect submissions
coverage_sweep.reason: Static trace (not executed): for a fixed set of plan files, each test's outcome is determined by fixed fixture bytes (SHA-checked) and a pure integer checker; the reference plans and an over-target or invalid plan therefore receive the same verdict on every clean run. Verifier fixture integrity mismatch would fail deterministically, not intermittently.

coverage_sweep.category: Candidate-influenced grading environment (env vars, cwd, caches)
coverage_sweep.reason: Verifier runs in a separate environment with python -I, no cacheprovider, fresh mktemp cwd; STAND_PLANS override is verifier-side only; only /app/plans artifacts are transferred.

rules: plan turn lists may be in any order
buffer rule between consecutive turns on a stand
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: A plan listing a stand's turns out of arrival order: check_plan sorts occupancy before pairwise buffer check, so the verdict is identical to the sorted listing.

rules: verifier day copies (gzip) must equal /app/days files
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Every run decompresses the same gzip bytes and asserts SHA-256 equal to roster; roster hashes match manifest hashes of environment day files, so cost and target inputs are identical across runs.

rules: cost is a sum of integer products
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Reference plans sit exactly on targets; with exact integer arithmetic the equality boundary cannot flip between runs due to summation order.

rules: solution search uses seeded RNG and wall-clock budget
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: solve.sh copies saved plans and never invokes search.py, so the Oracle's submitted bytes are constant across runs.
